sentences.text: An electrode is the sensor contacting the skin.
A cable connects it to the recording system.
An E C G lead is a calculated view of the heart's electrical activity, not simply the wire.
A standard twelve-lead E C G uses ten electrodes to create twelve views.
Six are limb-lead views, and six are chest-lead views.
Keep those counts separate before placing anything on the body.

scene.detail: Actual registered BodyParts3D thorax and existing Lead Placement Lab markers. Patient-right/left refer to the patient; front-view viewer left is patient RIGHT. The 50 source meshes include skin, sternum, clavicles, 12 rib pairs, costal cartilage and pectoralis; no heart, lungs, cable hardware or full limbs are present. Chest positions and intercostal overlays are derived reference-atlas teaching anchors, not measurements for an individual. The four limb labels point toward external limb regions, not validated diagnostic recording sites. This is a static anatomical/polarity lesson, with no ECG signal, contact-impedance or vector-projection solver. Lead RA/LA are electrode labels, not right/left atria. Any visible RL “GND” is the existing module’s teaching shorthand: the right-leg electrode commonly provides a common reference/driven-right-leg function; it is not a positive/negative measurement pole or necessarily literal earth ground. The unused RA/LA/LL electrode is never reassigned as ground. The skin sensor is represented only by a teaching placement marker; contact mechanics and hardware are not modeled.

sentences.text: Lead one compares the left arm with the right arm.
Lead two compares the left leg with the right arm.
Lead three compares the left leg with the left arm.
The first location named is positive in each comparison.
The remaining limb electrode does not become the ground for that lead.
A separate right-leg electrode commonly provides a reference or driven-right-leg function in the recording system.

sentences.text: The augmented limb leads are a V R, a V L, and a V F.
They view the heart from the right arm, left arm, and left leg, using calculated references.
Together with leads one, two, and three, they show the frontal plane.
Chest leads V one through V six view the heart in the transverse plane, each relative to a combined reference.
The word unipolar is traditional shorthand; a voltage measurement still requires a comparison.

sentences.text: Use the patient's landmarks, not guessed distances.
The sternal angle helps identify the second rib; the second intercostal space lies just below it.
From there, count down.
The midclavicular line descends from the midpoint of the clavicle.
The anterior axillary line and midaxillary line descend from the front and middle of the armpit.
There are twelve pairs of ribs and eleven intercostal spaces on each side.

sentences.text: Good recordings depend on reliable skin contact, secure electrodes, correct positions, and a relaxed, still subject.
Movement, muscle activity, loose contacts, and electrical interference can distort a tracing.
Limb-electrode colors vary by standard, so read the labels instead of relying on a color mnemonic alone.
Torso placements used for continuous monitoring are not automatically equivalent to standard diagnostic limb placements.
Follow the particular recording protocol rather than treating every configuration as interchangeable.

sentences.text: A lead records the projection of the heart's changing electrical activity onto that lead's axis.
A depolarization wave moving toward its positive pole usually creates a positive deflection; moving away usually creates a negative one.
A near-perpendicular net vector can produce a small or biphasic complex.
An isoelectric segment does not prove that every heart cell is electrically inactive.
Opposing signals or little net change can also produce a near-flat line.

sentences.text: The usual adult frontal Q R S axis reference is minus thirty to plus ninety degrees.
Leads one and a V F give a quick quadrant screen.
Both positive generally fits the normal quadrant.
Lead one positive with a V F negative is not automatically left axis deviation: the axis may still lie between zero and minus thirty degrees.
Lead two helps distinguish that borderline-normal region from a more leftward axis.
Axis is a clue, not a diagnosis by itself.
